turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Please come in and sit comfortably. It is quite warm outside, you must be tired from the waiting. What has been going on with you?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you, doctor. I am sorry to trouble you. I have come regarding my stomach, and for some months I am having bloating and loose motions after milk and ice cream.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): I am glad you came. Umm, tell me, how does it actually feel when it starts?

[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): The stomach becomes tight and full, doctor, and then within an hour or two I have loose motions, two or three times. It is only after milk or ice cream, not with every meal.
[SEG0005] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Doctor, she is not telling the full thing. She sleeps very badly, tossing about the whole night. And she does not take her calcium tablets on Sundays.

[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): If I may correct that, kindly. I sleep adequately, I only wake once on some nights, I would not call it bad sleep. And the calcium I miss on Saturday, not Sunday, only Saturday.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Alright, thank you both. We will take it slowly. Anjali, when did this stomach trouble first begin? Can you place it?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): It is hard to say exactly. Since Diwali, or maybe after Diwali. I cannot, uh, give you a proper date.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): That is perfectly fine, we do not need the exact day. Has your weight changed at all in this time?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): No, doctor. There has been no weight loss. My clothes fit the same.
[SEG0011] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I stay with her and I cook. I have not seen her become thin.
[SEG0012] person_1 (DOCTOR): Good to hear. The calcium tablets, what is the name, and how were you asked to take them?

[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): It is shellcal, five hundred mg, once a day, by mouth, after breakfast, for my bones. I have been on it since last winter, or the winter before that. I truly cannot remember which.
[SEG0014] person_1 (DOCTOR): So most days you take it, and you leave it out on Saturday. Is that the pattern?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, doctor. Saturday only. The other days I take it properly.
[SEG0016] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Sorry, I had said Sunday. Err, I mixed the days up. Saturday is correct.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): No harm done. Any other medicines just now? And any allergy to a medicine or a food?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No other medicines, doctor. And no allergies. None that I know of.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): You mentioned milk and ice cream. Did you try keeping off them for a stretch?

[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. I avoided milk and ice cream for one week, and the bloating was much less. Then at my cousin's function I took a little ice cream, and the same evening it all returned.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mm. And these days, are you still taking milk most of the time, or have you cut it down?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): I have mostly stopped, doctor. But I do slip now and then, and the loose motions come only on those days itself.
[SEG0023] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She had a small cut on her finger last month, from the kitchen knife. It healed in five days, quite normally. I thought you should know.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): Thank you for that. Any wounds that heal slowly? Any fever? Any blood in the motions?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): No, doctor. Nothing slow to heal, the cut was fine in five days. No fever, and no blood in the motions.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): How is your energy through the day? And is there tummy pain with the bloating, or only the fullness and the loose motions?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): My energy is alright, doctor. There is no real pain. Only the bloating and the loose motions.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right. Let me check the blood pressure and pulse. 122 over 78, and the pulse is 76. Comfortable.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): That is a relief. At a camp last year it was higher, though I do not remember the figure.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): We will go by today's reading. Lie back a moment, I will feel your tummy. It is soft, a little distended, and there is no tenderness.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, doctor. It feels full even now, and I took no milk today.

[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): From what you describe, this may well be lactose intolerance. It follows the milk and ice cream, and it settled when you stopped. I still would not want to miss coeliac disease.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Coeliac. I have only read the name, doctor. Is it something serious?
[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): It is worth excluding with a simple blood test. I am arranging coeliac serology, the tissue transglutaminase, to be taken today before you leave.
[SEG0035] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Should she stop every milk product till then? Even tea with a little milk?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): I do take tea with a small amount of milk. I am not sure that one bothers me as much as ice cream.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): For the next two weeks, kindly keep a diet diary. Note what you eat, especially milk, ice cream and tea, and what the stomach does afterwards.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Certainly, doctor. I will maintain it carefully.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): Please avoid large amounts of milk and ice cream until we review. If a little milk in tea does not upset you, just write it in the diary, no need for a total ban.
[SEG0040] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I can help her write it. She, umm, forgets by the evening sometimes.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): That is kind, but I would prefer to write it myself. I do not forget quite as much as she says.
[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): Either way is fine so long as it is honest. Come back in three weeks, and we will look at the blood result and the diary together.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you, doctor. Three weeks will suit me. Should I take the shellcal on Saturdays also, from now?

[SEG0044] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yes, take it every day, Saturday included, after breakfast, the way it was meant. If the motions ever show blood, or you feel faint, do not wait, come sooner. Otherwise I will see you in three weeks.

spec.situation: Person with bloating and loose stools after milk and ice cream for months, no weight loss; tried to avoid dairy for a week; blood test for coeliac planned; diet diary asked.

traps.happens: A caregiver or relative reports observations ('the cut healed in five days', 'she sleeps badly', 'he does not take the tablets on Sundays'); the patient agrees, disagrees or corrects one point. The nurse also reports a measurement that the patient mentioned before.
traps.label_rule: reported_by follows who said it. A healing cut that healed normally is a negative finding (no slow-healing wounds) or nothing, NOT a symptom. A disputed fact is recorded with certainty disputed or as an uncertainty. A correction replaces the earlier value (Saturday, not Sunday).

features: vague_dates: the patient cannot date things ('since Diwali or after', 'last winter, or the one before'); no invented date; a date_uncertain item.
relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.

omissions.text: No other medicines currently besides Shelcal.
No known food allergies as well as no medicine allergies.
Loose motions occur only on the same days she slips and takes milk/ice cream, not otherwise.
Patient reports current fullness/bloating even on the examination day despite having had no milk that day.
Caregiver-reported finger cut last month from a kitchen knife healed normally in five days; patient confirmed the cut healed fine in five days.
Doctor advised review in three weeks specifically to go over both the blood test result and the diet diary together.
